title: Traffic & Quota Explorer — concepts and quick sketches (WIP)
content:
Purpose
---
Working doc capturing early UX concepts for a unified Traffic & Quota Explorer focused on per-key and per-route attribution. Goal: help developers and platform owners answer:
- Who is using which route (and which API key) right now?
- Which keys are bumping up against soft/hard quotas? Which routes cause the largest token spend?
- Where should we apply quota fences vs. rate-limit tuning to reduce tail latencies and cost?

Audience
---
Primary: Platform engineers, SREs, Product owners for customers on Dedicated/Private, and larger teams using multiple credentials. Secondary: internal Support/CS for debugging customer quota incidents.

High-level problems we want to solve
---
1) Quick triage: from alert -> identity -> action (throttle, block, increase quota, contact owner).
2) Cost visibility: per-key unit economics (tokens, compute tier, model variant usage).
3) Behavioral patterns: route shapes (burstiness, steady streams, spiky tails) so we can recommend batching/caching or different plan tiers.
4) Guardrails: surface keys close to quota and suggest temporary fallbacks (lower-cap models, disable streaming).

Key UX surfaces proposed
---
A. Overview dashboard (top-level)
- Snapshot row: active keys, routes with errors, percent of keys above 75% quota, tokens/min to 99th percentile latency correlation.
- Small multiples: last 24h / last 7d / last 30d toggle.
- Global heatmap: route x key (aggregated) showing concentrated spend hotspots (hover ink shows top 3 callers).

B. Key detail flyout (click on a credential)
- Header: key name, owner, tier, quota bucket, last rotated.
- Timeline: tokens/day, requests/day, 95/99 latency overlays.
- Breakdown row: top 10 routes by token consumption and by request count (separate columns).
- Anomaly band: automatic detection of sudden 3x increases week-over-week with one-click create-incident.
- Suggested actions: throttle profile templates (sustained qps cap, burst cap, token-limit per-minute), plus a preview mode to simulate expected cost decrease.

C. Route detail page
- Route definition text (method + path) and sample request + response snippet.
- Attribution by credential: stacked bars showing which keys drive which percent of tokens. Click to filter to a single key.
- Token footprint breakdown: prompt vs completion (if available), model variant distribution (gpt-3.5 vs optimized-small), quantization impact.

D. Quota fencing view (policy builder)
- Visual builder for per-key/per-route quotas: time window, token cap, sliding-window vs fixed-window, soft vs hard limit and automated escalation (notify, throttle, block).
- Simulate button: runs replay on 7d sample and shows estimated rate-limit hits / blocked requests.

E. Alerting & Exports
- Per-key alerts for approaching quotas (75%, 90%, 98%). Alerts include top offending route and suggested mitigation.
- Export CSV/JSON of recent requests (sanitized) for offline analysis.

Wireframe notes (textual sketches)
---
- Overview: left rail list of top 20 keys (sorted by tokens last 24h) with microbars showing trend. Center workspace is heatmap; right side a small inspector.
- Heatmap cell click -> small modal with quick actions (throttle, add quota fence, open ticket).
- Colors: use palette to indicate severity (blue: normal, amber: approaching, red: over). Patterning: diagonal stripes + red to indicate quota-exceeded cells (so small printouts still readable).

Behavior and data model implications
---
- Need event-level sampling for heavy customers (store 1 in N requests + full aggregates).
- Pre-aggregate keys x routes hourly to render heatmap quickly. Rollup pipeline to include tokens (prompt/completion), model, latency.
- Keep last 90 days of aggregates; raw sampled traces for 7 days.

Backlog (initial, prioritized)
---
1) P0 - Heatmap + key list + quick inspector (MVP): build hourly aggregates & render heatmap. (Est: 3 sprints)
2) P0 - Key detail flyout with top-10 routes and one-click throttle templates. (Est: 2 sprints)
3) P1 - Quota fencing policy builder + simulate (needs replay infra). (Est: 3 sprints)
4) P1 - Route detail (route attribution + model variant breakdown). (Est: 2 sprints)
5) P2 - Alerts and recommended mitigations integration with Console notifications + PagerDuty. (Est: 2 sprints)
6) P2 - Export and raw-request sampling UI. (Est: 1 sprint)

Open questions / decisions
---
- Sampling rate defaults: what provides good debugging vs cost? Proposal: 1 in 100 for Hosted; 1 in 10 for Dedicated customers by default, adjustable per-customer.
- How to present sensitive request payloads? Default sanitize, allow opt-in for full payloads with audit log.
- Soft vs hard quota UX: should soft limit auto-suggest rate-limits or leave manual? Proposal: show one-click suggested throttle but require explicit enable by owner.
- Multi-tenant heatmap scaling: for customers with 10k keys, heatmap should show top-N + aggregated tail. Threshold heuristics needed.

Quick mock interactions (user flows)
---
Flow A: Support gets alert for high token spend -> opens Explorer -> sorts keys by rise % -> selects key -> views top route -> applies temporary throttle template -> monitors 1h -> marks incident resolved.
Flow B: Platform engineer wants to reduce cost for a customer -> opens route detail -> sees majority tokens from streaming endpoint -> suggests fallback to non-streaming for non-interactive ingestion routes -> creates rollout note and quota fence to protect other users.

Acceptance criteria (MVP heatmap + key flyout)
---
- Heatmap renders in < 2s for customers with up to 5000 keys (after aggregates).
- Clicking a cell opens flyout with top-10 routes within 500ms.
- Playbook: from alert to throttle applied < 5 minutes (UI + backend path validated).

Notes for frontend engineers
---
- Use canvas for heatmap with progressive render and tooltips; fallback to SVG grid for small results.
- Client should fetch hourly aggregates and also stream small delta events for realtime ink.
- Provide design tokens for severity states to match Console theme.

Next steps / meetings
---
- Sync with Observability on aggregates schema (Ethan, Maya) — schedule 11/12.
- Spike: replay infra cost estimate (SRE + infra) — 1 week spike.
- Usability test with 3 CS reps using high-volume customer replay — target before EOW 12/05.

Todo (short)
---
- [ ] Create interactive prototype (Figma) of heatmap + flyout (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft API for aggregates (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Open JIRA epic and link to this doc (owner: Priya)

Random ideas captured (brainstorm)
---
- \"What-if\" slider: if we cap key X to N tokens/min, show expected change in 99 latency and blocked reqs.
- Integrate with Optimize: recommend quantization/model changes when large token spend ties to a small number of routes.
- Onboarding checklist for new customers: enable Explorer, sampling defaults, quota templates.

References / links
---
- Related console files: quota-decomposition-journey-mapping-wip, per-route-deep-dive-playbook (see Drive).
- Jira: JIRA-INF-778 (heatmap backend epic).

End of doc.
